messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rebecca Li <rebecca.li@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO follow-up — Private VPC network (ACME)

Hi Rebecca — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our call and the network stuff we need to qualify for Private VPC/on-prem deployment: 

1) SLO targets you shared: p50 ~ 60ms, p95 < 120ms, p99 goal < 200ms for single-request latency (inference-only, streaming disabled). You also said a streaming mode is required for chat use cases (SSE) with target tail latency for first token < 150ms.

2) Throughput/concurrency: expected peak concurrency ~ 120 concurrent requests (50 token average) and sustained throughput ~ 400 req/min. Bursts up to 300 concurrent for short windows.

3) Network topology items we need from your infra team to finalize the qualification:
   - Public egress IPs (if traffic leaves ACME network) or confirmation that we can set up VPC peering / transit gateway.
   - VPN / direct connect details (latency + MTU) and whether any TCP proxies/load balancers terminate in front of the inference hosts.
   - RTT and packet loss baselines between ACME app tier (where SDK runs) and the planned Redwood Private egress/ingress endpoints. We typically ask for 3x 1-minute iperf3 runs during peak/off-peak to capture variance.
   - Any TLS interception, IDS/IPS appliances, or proxying that could add head-of-line latency (we've seen 10–30ms added in some stacks).

4) Test artifacts we can provide: a small load script (k6/iperf3) + a sample 512-token prompt bundle + a lightweight streaming client to exercise SSE.

Next steps I propose:
- Rebecca/ACME infra to share egress IPs or open peering ticket by EOD Tue (4/6).
- ACME runs iperf3 and shares results (3 runs) by end of next week.
- Schedule 60-min tech deep-dive (network + concurrency tuning) — can Jordan + Jonas join? I blocked a few slots: Thu 4/8 10am PDT or Fri 4/9 1pm PDT.

I've attached a short network-trace template for the iperf3/tracepath results to make it quick.

Thanks — Marissa

--

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few clarifications / answers from our side: 

• SLOs: the p99 < 200ms is what our product PM is pushing for as well for non-streaming. For streaming chat, the requirement is first-token < 200ms (we may be able to relax to 250ms if needed).

• Throughput: our backend service will multiplex requests; the 120 concurrent baseline is accurate. Bursts can be higher during marketing events.

• Network: we can provide public egress IPs for now (temporary) and we are opening a ticket with our network team to explore VPC peering/direct connect. I can share the egress IP list by EOD Monday 4/5.

• iperf3: happy to run 3x 1-minute runs. We will include tests from two app subnets (us-east-1a and us-east-1c).

• We do have an enterprise proxy in front of outbound traffic that can add ~10–20ms; I will confirm whether we can bypass for the test.

Let's book Thu 4/8 10am PDT — that works for Jordan and me. Please send calendar invite.

—Rebecca

Looping our infra/ops folks — ACME is targeting p99 < 200ms non-streaming and first-token ~150–250ms for streaming. Key asks from us for qualification are in Marissa's note (iperf3 runs, egress IPs / peering, proxy details).

Jonas / Vivek — can you weigh in on the acceptable network budgets and any config we want to recommend on the ACME side to hit these numbers? Two quick thoughts:

1) If RTT from ACME app tier to Redwood Private edge is >40ms we will likely see trouble meeting p99 <200ms at higher concurrencies without local batching adjustments or moving inference closer. We should provide guidance for TCP keepalive and Nagle (we recommend keepalive 30s, disable Nagle for streaming RPC).

2) For streaming: SSE is sensitive to head-of-line blocking. If they have proxies that aggregate/inspect traffic, advise bypass for streaming endpoints or use TCP keepalives + smaller chunk sizes.

Also attaching a sample load profile and the minimal packet-capture steps we'd like them to run (packet capture + tracepath + iperf3).

--Jordan

1) ACME (Rebecca): share temporary egress IP list by EOD Mon 2027-04-05 + run 3x 1-minute iperf3 runs from us-east-1a and us-east-1c and upload results to the Drive link.
2) ACME (Carlos): confirm whether the enterprise proxy can be bypassed for streaming traffic or provide the proxy latency numbers (avg / p95).
3) Redwood (Jordan / Jonas / Vivek): we'll prepare a short network playbook (recommended TCP settings, MTU guidance, SSE tuning) and a runbook for the iperf3/pcap captures. Expect that by Tue 2027-04-06.
4) Schedule tech deep-dive Thu 2027-04-08 10:00am PDT — calendar invite sent.

If the iperf3 RTTs show >40ms RTT or packet loss >0.5% we will propose one of the following mitigations:
 - route inference via a closer regional edge (we can stand up a regional Private edge in us-east-1)
 - use an on-prem inference appliance (on-prem node) to reduce network hops
 - apply predictive client-side batching to reduce per-request variance (client SDK change)

Carlos / Rebecca — once you upload the iperf3 results we'll do an initial pass and reply within 24 hours with whether the baseline meets our latency SLOs or whether we need a short mitigation plan.

Thanks — Marissa
